research_question: Does the current motion-weighted/adaptive sampling strategy itself hurt Gemini ASL translation compared with uniform temporal sampling, holding target density and all other inference conditions fixed?
scope: 12 fixed diagnostic clips only (diagnostic_12_clips.json) - not the full 40-clip taxonomy, not the 128-clip benchmark

arm_A_existing_baseline.description: Existing production-equivalent sampler: motion-weighted/adaptive timestamp allocation (run_current_model.allocate_timestamps).

arm_B_new_controlled_arm.description: New ablation config, added to asl-translator/asl-eval/run_current_model.py CONFIGS additively. Identical to Arm A in every knob EXCEPT sampling_strategy.
arm_B_new_controlled_arm.sampling_strategy: uniform (run_current_model.allocate_timestamps_uniform - evenly spaced across the observed clip span, ignores motion energy entirely, preserves chronological ordering)
arm_B_new_controlled_arm.predictions_output: asl-translator/evaluation/diagnostics/phase1_temporal_ablation/controlled_ablation/adaptive_vs_uniform_2fps/predictions/ - NEW real Gemini calls, this experiment only

single_controlled_variable: timestamp allocation formula (motion-weighted vs. evenly-spaced). Frame budget, model, prompt, batch size, dedup, thinking_level, and target_frames_per_sec are identical between arms for every clip.

design_check_summary.source: design_check.json (same directory) - LOCAL ONLY, no model calls, produced before any inference
design_check_summary.note_on_min_frame_budget: For 8 of the 12 clips, duration_s * 2.0 < 24, so MIN_FRAME_BUDGET=24 is the binding constraint and the ACTUAL sampling density is higher than a literal 2 frames/sec for BOTH arms equally (same duration, same budget_mode, so this affects Arm A and Arm B identically - not a confound between arms, but means '2fps' is not literally true for these 8 clips). See design_check.json per_clip[].min_frame_budget_binding and naive_literal_2fps_frame_count vs. frame_budget.
design_check_summary.confound_check_result: No major confound identified that would prevent a fair adaptive-vs-uniform comparison on these 12 clips: frame counts match exactly (0 mismatches), timestamp ordering is chronological in both arms, and every other inference condition (model, prompt, batch size, dedup, thinking_level, target density) is identical.

adaptive_production_sampler_unchanged: run_current_model.allocate_timestamps() and every existing CONFIGS entry are byte-for-byte unmodified; the uniform path is purely additive (new function allocate_timestamps_uniform, new CONFIGS entry, new sampling_strategy branch gated on cfg.get('sampling_strategy')).
